chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Suleym the freedman of Tarbaal, who said: Hisham narrated to me from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The people are upon six categories.'
He said: I said, 'Do you permit me to write it down?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'What shall I write?' He said, 'Write: The people of threat are from the people of Paradise and the people of Hell.'
And write: And others have confessed their sins, they have mingled a good deed and an evil one.
He said: I said, 'Who are these?' He said, 'Wahshi is among them.'
And write: And others are those of whom delay is made, awaiting Allah's command; whether He will punish them or turn to them (mercifully).
He said: And write: Except the weak from among the men and the women and the children, who have not the power to find a way.
They cannot find a way to disbelief, nor can they find a way to faith; so these, it may be, Allah will pardon them.
He said: And write: The people of Al-Araf.

I said, 'And what are the people of Al-Araf?' He said: 'A people whose good deeds and evil deeds are equal. So if He enters them into the Fire, it is due to their sins, and if He enters them into Paradise, it is due to His Mercy.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْأَعْرَافِ: The people of Al-Araf (a barrier or elevated place between Paradise and Hell)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْوَعِيدِ: People of threat (those promised punishment but may be forgiven)
key_terms.الْوَحْشِيُّ: Wahshi (the killer of Hamza, cited as an example of mixed deeds)

ai.seo_question: What are the six categories of people and their fates according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) categorizes humanity into six groups, offering a nuanced Shia eschatology that balances divine justice with mercy. This classification highlights the unique status of the 'People of Al-Araf' (Ahl al-A'raf), whose equal good and bad deeds place them in a liminal state awaiting God's final decree, and the 'Murj'ah', whose fate is suspended between punishment and forgiveness. The inclusion of Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, among those who mixed deeds illustrates the profound capacity for repentance even for major sinners, while the 'Mustad'afin' (weak) are excused due to their inability to comprehend or choose the path of faith.

en.hubeali:
Anumber of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Suleym a slave of Tarbaal who said, 
‘Hisham narrated to me, from Hamza Bin Al-Tayyar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The people are upon three categories’.

I said, ‘Would you<sup>asws</sup> permit me that I write this down?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘What shall I write?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Promised people would be from the inhabitants of the Paradise and the inhabitants of the Fire.
And write [9:102] And others have confessed their sins, they have mingled a good deed and an evil one; maybe Allah will Turn to them (Mercifully)’.

Heasws said: ‘And write [4:98] Except the weak from among the men and the children who have not in their power the means nor can they find a way (to escape) [4:99] So these, it may be, Allah will Pardon them’.
Heasws said: ‘And write [7:48] And the the people of Al-Araf’. I said, ‘And what are the the people of Al-Araf?’

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘A people whose good deeds and their evils deeds would be equal. So if they were to be entered into the Fire, it would be due to their sins, and if they were to be entered into the Paradise, it would be due to His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mercy’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Sulaym Mawla Tirbal who has said the Hisham narrated to him from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said to me, ‘People are of six categories.’

I then asked, ‘Can I write them down?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, you can do so.’ I then asked, ‘What should I write?’ The Imam said, ‘Write down: the people promised paradise and those warned against the fire (but ignored it).
Write down, “. . . others of them have already confessed their sins and have mixed virtuous deeds with sinful ones.’” [9:102]
I then asked, ‘Who are such people?’ The Imam said, ‘Wahshi (assassin of Hamza) is one of them.’
The Imam said, ‘Write down, “There are others who have no good deeds for which they may receive any reward or sins for which they may be punished. . . .” [9:106]

The Imam said, ‘Write down, “As for the really weak and oppressed men, women, and children who were not able to find any means of obtaining their freedom or of having the right guidance, [4:98] [are not able to do anything against the unbelievers or find the right guidance] perhaps Allah will forgive them; He is All-merciful and All- forgiving.” [4:99]
The Imam said, ‘Write down the people of ‘A’raf.’

I asked, ‘Who are they?’ The Imam said, ‘They are the people whose good and bad deeds measure equally. If they will be sent to the fire it will be due to their sins and if they will be sent to paradise it will be due to His kindness.’”
